jobs.statement: When the capped default rate moves and the bill changes, help a household bill payer choose between locking a price and staying flexible while they cannot absorb an unpredictable bill and do not trust a comparison they cannot check.
jobs.struggling_moment: The bill or monthly payment changes after a cap change and the household does not know whether acting or waiting costs them more (source-004, source-005, source-013).
jobs.desired_progress: A defensible decision to fix, move to a wholesale-linked deal, or stay, with a way to check the arithmetic for their own usage and region.
workarounds: doing nothing and remaining on the default rate (source-005)

push: visible unit rate and standing charge increases (source-005)
pull: deals advertised several percent below the cap (source-012)

criteria: total annual cost for my usage and region (source-005, source-012)

post_purchase_and_negative_cases: job-006 and parts of job-002 and job-005 are post-purchase or adoption jobs, not acquisition jobs. A brand-named support question is post-purchase, not bottom-of-funnel.
Negative case for the fix decision: the regulator states that already-fixed customers are unaffected by cap changes, so a share of the population has no job here at all (source-005).
Negative case for export: households without export-capable metering cannot act at all until metering changes (source-002).
